title: Your path to production
idea: A backend is the part of an app users never see but always depend on. This book takes you from JavaScript basics to a deployed, scalable service.

analogy.text: A restaurant: the dining room is the frontend, the kitchen is the backend. Guests judge the meal, but the kitchen decides whether it arrives.
analogy.breaks: Unlike a kitchen, a backend serves thousands of tables at once, all day.

points: Each page is one idea, split into a few short frames.
Press → to step through. Press ? to see every shortcut.
Edit and run code right on the page.
Stuck? Ask the tutor. It already knows the page you are on.

quiz.q: Which part of an app is the backend?
quiz.why: The backend runs on servers: it stores data, applies rules and answers requests.

takeaway: Learn the path in order: language, services, trust, production.

starters: What does a backend engineer actually do?
Why use Node.js for the backend?
Give me a four-week study plan

pitfalls: Reading alone will not stick; edit and run the code yourself.
Do not skip JavaScript: every later chapter builds on it.
